Plot a selIndex Object

Source: R/plot.selIndex.R
plot.selIndex.Rd

Produces one of three diagnostic plots for a selIndex result.

"index" (default)

Caterpillar-style plot of lines sorted by index value, coloured by selection status. Expected genetic gain per environment is annotated inside the plot.

"heatmap"

For multivariate objects only. A lines \(\times\) environments tile heatmap of raw GEBVs. Rows (lines) are sorted by index rank (rank 1 at top); columns are environments in trait-level order. Cell colour encodes GEBV magnitude: pt.col[1] (steelblue) = high, pt.col[2] (firebrick) = low, white = overall median. A dashed horizontal rule separates selected from unselected lines. Reveals broad vs specific adaptation at a glance: uniformly blue top rows indicate broadly adapted candidates; blue in some columns but not others signals environment-specific performers.

"weights"

Horizontal lollipop chart of the index weights \(\mathbf{b}\), coloured steelblue (positive) or firebrick (negative). Communicates the derived combining weights for Smith-Hazel and desired-gains indices back to the breeder.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'selIndex'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("index", "heatmap", "weights"),
  prop.select = 0.1,
  threshold = NULL,
  pt.col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
  pt.cex = 0.9,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A "selIndex" object returned by selIndex.

type

Character string. One of "index" (default), "heatmap", or "weights".

prop.select

Numeric proportion of lines to flag as selected. Default 0.10.

threshold

Numeric threshold applied to the index. If between 0 and 1 exclusive, treated as a quantile; otherwise a raw index value. If NULL (default) prop.select is used.

pt.col

Character vector of length 2: selected / high-GEBV colour (pt.col[1]) and unselected / low-GEBV colour (pt.col[2]). Default c("steelblue", "firebrick").

pt.cex

Numeric point size (used by type = "index" only). Default 0.9.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

selIndex, print.selIndex, summary.selIndex

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
si <- selIndex(gp.mv, weights = c(Trial1 = 2, Trial2 = 1))
plot(si)                              # ranked index (caterpillar)
plot(si, type = "heatmap")            # lines x environments GEBV heatmap
plot(si, type = "weights")            # index weight bar chart
} # }
